reason: The text fragment contains only two named characters: Moses (משה) and Aaron (אהרן). Both are depicted as divinely appointed leaders receiving direct commandments from God and serving as intermediaries between God and the Israelites. They are portrayed in exceptional, authoritative roles rather than as regular, ordinary people. While the passage references many groups of regular people (the Israelites, slaves, residents, hired workers, sojourners), these are collective references without individual names or characterizations.
